  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has sourced evidence that platforms already pay for proof-of-human verification. not.bot charges $9.99–$249/mo and useHUMA up to $499/mo, with public pricing pages. Idea B admits no one has ever been shown paying for Free Pascal/Lazarus documentation.",
    "Idea A names a self-serve path a solo founder could reach within 90 days: small marketplaces, dating apps and review sites, via a low-cost developer launch. Banks and Zoom-scale buyers sit outside that window. Idea B's only channels are unpaid forum posting and generic paid search, aimed at an audience the brief itself calls too small.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence ties pain to money lost: a $243,000 deepfake-authorized wire and a dating user who sent money to a bot. Idea B's evidence shows frustration with documentation, two of its three quotes are from 2010 and roughly 2013, and none shows willingness to pay.",
    "Idea B's own case against points to a blocker no outside product can fix: maintainers unwilling to engage with doc fixes. Idea A's risks are serious but can be navigated. Crowded free tiers and biometric regulation (BIPA/GDPR) can be partly addressed by choosing a narrow niche and avoiding biometric signals."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's payer and price hypothesis. The ~$50/month business tier is anchored only to Read the Docs' generic Business pricing, not to any Pascal or Lazarus buyer. The one institutional payer named, the Free Pascal and Lazarus Foundation, is documented as funding development, not docs. No company shipping a commercial Lazarus product is shown wanting or buying such a tier.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderately high confidence that A is the better first bet, mainly because B has no evidenced payer at all. A is far from strong. Its reachable self-serve segment has at least four competitors with free tiers or low entry prices, and these push pricing toward zero. Its enterprise segments need 6–18 month sales cycles or are already served. None of its demand quotes come from a platform buyer saying they would pay a new entrant. A first paying customer within 90 days is plausible for A but not demonstrated."
}
